facts.statement: Beipiaosaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Barremian age.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous (Barremian)

facts.statement: The first remains of Beipiaosaurus were discovered in 1996 and formally described in 1999.
facts.quote: The first remains were found in 1996 and formally described in 1999.

facts.statement: Before Yutyrannus was discovered, Beipiaosaurus were considered among the heaviest dinosaurs known to have direct evidence of feathers.
facts.quote: Before the discovery of Yutyrannus, Beipiaosaurus were among the heaviest dinosaurs known from direct evidence to be feathered.

facts.statement: Three distinct specimens of Beipiaosaurus have been reported.
facts.quote: Beipiaosaurus is known from three reported specimens.

facts.statement: Preserved feather impressions allowed researchers to determine that Beipiaosaurus had brownish plumage.
facts.quote: Numerous impressions of feather structures were preserved that allowed researchers to determine the feathering color which turned out to be brownish.

facts.statement: Beipiaosaurus were small therizinosaurs, reaching about 2.2 meters in length and weighing approximately 27 kilograms.
facts.quote: They were relatively small-sized therizinosaurs, measuring 2.2 m long and weighing about 27 kg in contrast to the advanced and giant Segnosaurus or Therizinosaurus.

facts.statement: Unlike other therizinosaurids which typically have four toes, Beipiaosaurus had a three-toed foot.
facts.quote: Also, their feet configuration differs from therizinosaurids, having a generic three-toed pes instead of four as seen in other members.

facts.statement: A partial skeleton of Beipiaosaurus was discovered in 1996 by a farmer named Li Yinxian near the village of Sihetun.
facts.quote: In 1996, a farmer, Li Yinxian discovered a partial skeleton of a theropod dinosaur near the village of Sihetun.

facts.statement: The species Beipiaosaurus inexpectus was named and described by Xu Xing, Tang Zhilu, and Wang Xiaolin, with the discovery announced in Nature on May 27, 1999.
facts.quote: On 27 May 1999, the discovery was announced in the academic journal Nature and the type species Beipiaosaurus inexpectus named and described by Xu Xing, Tang Zhilu and Wang Xiaolin.

facts.statement: The name Beipiaosaurus means "Beipiao lizard," named after the city of Beipiao near the fossil discovery site.
facts.quote: The generic name Beipiaosaurus translates as "Beipiao lizard" after Beipiao, a city in China near the location of its discovery.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen (IVPP V11559) was recovered from the Jianshangou Beds of the Yixian Formation in Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: The holotype (type specimen) of Beipiaosaurus inexpectus, IVPP V11559, was recovered in the Jianshangou Beds of the Yixian Formation in Liaoning Province, China.

facts.statement: A third specimen, labeled BMNHC PH000911, was mentioned in a 2014 study by Li et al.
facts.quote: Li et al. 2014 mentioned a third specimen labelled under the number BMNHC PH000911.

facts.statement: The largest known specimen of Beipiaosaurus is estimated to be 2.2 meters long.
facts.quote: Beipiaosaurus was a small therizinosaur, with the largest specimen having an estimated length of 2.2 m.

facts.statement: In 2013, Zanno and Makovicky estimated the body mass of Beipiaosaurus at around 27 kilograms based on femur length.
facts.quote: In 2013, Lindsay E. Zanno and Peter Makovicky estimated its body mass at around 27 kg, based on the length of its femur.

facts.statement: In 2024, Gregory S. Paul estimated Beipiaosaurus' body length at 1.8 meters and its mass at around 50 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2024, Gregory S. Paul estimated Beipiaosaurus' body length at 1.8 m, and its body mass at around 50 kg.

facts.statement: The presence of reduced inner toes in Beipiaosaurus suggests that the four-toed condition of advanced therizinosaurids evolved from a three-toed ancestor.
facts.quote: More advanced therizinosaurids have four functional toes, but the feet of Beipiaosaurus still have reduced inner toes, showing that the derived therizinosaurid condition may have evolved from a three-toed therizinosauroid ancestor.

facts.statement: Beipiaosaurus had a large head relative to other therizinosaurs, with a lower jaw roughly the same length as the femur.
facts.quote: The head was large relative to other therizinosaurs, with the lower jaw measuring about same length as the femur.

facts.statement: A 2003 study detailed the pygostyle of Beipiaosaurus, suggesting its original function was not linked to pennaceous feathers.
facts.quote: In 2003 the pygostyle, consisting of the fused five last vertebrae of the tail, was described in greater detail, suggesting that the original function of the pygostyle was not linked with pennaceous feathers.

facts.statement: The skull of Beipiaosaurus was proportionally large compared to other therizinosaurs.
facts.quote: The skull of Beipiaosaurus was fairly large, proportionally, compared to other therizinosaurs.

facts.statement: Preserved teeth are homodont and leaf-shaped with denticles, though it is unclear if front teeth were enlarged and conical like in other therizinosaurs.
facts.quote: The preserved teeth are fairly homodont (even in size and shape), and folidont (leaf-shaped with prominent denticles), though it is not clear whether those near the front of the dentary were enlarged and conidont (conical and with reduced denticles), as in other therizinosaurs.

facts.statement: Beipiaosaurus is classified as a genus of therizinosauroid theropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Beipiaosaurus is a genus of therizinosauroid theropod dinosaurs that lived in China during the Early Cretaceous in the Yixian Formation.

facts.statement: Features of Beipiaosaurus suggest that all therizinosauroids are coelurosaurian theropods, rather than sauropodomorphs or ornithischians.
facts.quote: Beipiaosaurus, being considered to be a primitive therizinosauroid, has features which suggest that all therizinosauroids, including the more derived Therizinosauridae, to be coelurosaurian theropods, not sauropodomorph or ornithischian relatives as once believed.

facts.statement: Therizinosaurs, including Beipiaosaurus, are generally considered herbivorous based on their prosauropod-like teeth and body structure.
facts.quote: The exact classification of therizinosaurs had in the past been hotly debated, since their prosauropod-like teeth and body structure indicate that they were generally herbivorous, unlike typical theropods.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the front teeth of Beipiaosaurus were enlarged and conical like those of other therizinosaurs.
facts.quote: though it is not clear whether those near the front of the dentary were enlarged and conidont (conical and with reduced denticles), as in other therizinosaurs.

facts.statement: Four incomplete cervical vertebrae have been preserved in the Beipiaosaurus fossil record.
facts.quote: Four of Beipiaosaurus' cervical (neck) vertebrae are preserved, all of them incompletely.

facts.statement: Researchers estimate that Beipiaosaurus likely had nine or ten cervical vertebrae based on comparisons with related species.
facts.quote: Based on Jianchangosaurus and STM 31-1, nine or ten were likely present.

facts.statement: Beipiaosaurus possessed low and undeveloped neural spines on its neck vertebrae, a trait shared with many other therizinosaurs.
facts.quote: The neural spines of the cervical vertebrae were low and undeveloped, like those of many other therizinosaurs.

facts.statement: Six dorsal vertebrae are preserved in the Beipiaosaurus holotype, with four articulated and two isolated.
facts.quote: Six dorsal (back) vertebrae are preserved, four of them articulated and exposed in lateral view, and the other two isolated and exposed in anterolateral (exposing the front and side) and lateral views.

facts.statement: The last four dorsal vertebrae of Beipiaosaurus were fused together.
facts.quote: The last four dorsal vertebrae were fused.

facts.statement: Thirty caudal vertebrae are preserved in the Beipiaosaurus specimen, though the animal likely had more.
facts.quote: The caudal (tail) series is represented by a total of thirty preserved vertebrae, though more were certainly present.

facts.statement: The tail vertebrae of Beipiaosaurus fused at the tip to form a pygostyle.
facts.quote: The vertebrae towards the tip of the caudal column were fused into a pygostyle.

facts.statement: The hand of Beipiaosaurus is fairly complete and characterized by slender phalanges.
facts.quote: The manus (hand) is fairly complete. It was overall slender, as were the phalanges (digit bones; finger bones, in this case).

facts.statement: Beipiaosaurus had long, recurved claws on its hands that were roughly equal in length to the finger bones.
facts.quote: The manual unguals (claws) were long and recurved, roughly equal in length to the phalanges they articulated to.

facts.statement: Unlike other therizinosaurs, the middle claw on the hand of Beipiaosaurus was the largest.
facts.quote: Unlike in other therizinosaurs, the middle manual ungual was the largest.

facts.statement: The ilium of Beipiaosaurus was parallelogram-shaped, resembling birds and dromaeosaurids but differing from later therizinosaurs.
facts.quote: The ilium of Beipiaosaurus was shaped like a parallelogram, similar to that of birds and dromaeosaurids, but unlike that of later therizinosaurs.

facts.statement: The first metatarsal of Beipiaosaurus was robust, did not touch the tarsus, and connected to the second metatarsal along its mid-shaft.
facts.quote: The first metatarsal was robust. It did not contact the tarsus, and articulated with the second metatarsal on the mid-shaft.

facts.statement: The holotype of Beipiaosaurus preserves short, slender filamentous feathers on its left arm.
facts.quote: The first feather impressions were found in the holotype specimen, consisting of short, slender filamentous feathers on the left arm.

facts.statement: Beipiaosaurus had 4–7 cm long parallel filaments on its tail, 1.5 mm wide, lacking pennaceous feathers or a tail fan.
facts.quote: The tail was also covered in feathers between 4–7 cm, consisting of parallel filaments with a width of 1.5 mm, without a trace of pennaceous feathers or a tail fan, as indicated by the preserved pygostyle.

facts.statement: Elongated broad filamentous feathers (EBFFs) were first described in 2009 by Xu and colleagues based on specimen STM 31-1.
facts.quote: These feathers, known as EBFFs (elongated broad filamentous feathers), were first described by Xu et al. 2009, based on specimen STM 31-1 consisting of the torso, head and neck.

facts.statement: The EBFFs of Beipiaosaurus measured 100–150 mm long, approximately half the length of its neck.
facts.quote: The EBFFs of Beipiaosaurus are also much longer than other primitive feather types, measuring about 100 - 150 mm long, roughly half the length of the neck.

facts.statement: The EBFFs of Beipiaosaurus were unusually broad, reaching up to 3 mm in width in the holotype.
facts.quote: The EBFFs of Beipiaosaurus are also unusually broad, up to 3 mm wide in the holotype.

facts.statement: Preserved EBFFs of Beipiaosaurus were fairly stiff, showing no curvature beyond a broad arc.
facts.quote: None of the preserved EBFFs were curved or bent beyond a broad arc in either specimen, indicating that they were fairly stiff.

facts.statement: A 2014 study by Li and colleagues analyzed melanosomes in 13 fossil specimens, including Beipiaosaurus, alongside 181 extant animals.
facts.quote: Li et al. 2014 compared the color and shape of the melanosomes in 181 extant animal specimens, 13 fossil specimens (including Beipiaosaurus) and previous data about the melanosome diversity using scanning electron microscopes.

facts.statement: Specimen BMNHC PH000911 of Beipiaosaurus preserves neck feathers with sphere-shaped melanosomes inferred to be dark brownish.
facts.quote: The examined specimen of Beipaosaurus, BMNHC PH000911, preserves feather impressions which are located in the neck area. These are filamentous/sparse in structure and the sampled melanosomes were sphere-shaped and inferred to have a brownish colouration like those in modern reptiles which fall within the range of dark brownish colourations.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the unique EBFFs of Beipiaosaurus and related early therizinosaurs were likely used for visual display.
facts.quote: These findings suggest that they might have been used for visual display and were common among early therizinosaurs.

facts.statement: Beipiaosaurus was definitively placed within the Theropoda, specifically as a maniraptoran, due to theropod features and feather impressions found in its holotype.
facts.quote: The description of Beipiaosaurus helped to assemble the definitive placement of therizinosaurs within the Theropoda, especially as maniraptorans thanks to the numerous theropod features and irrefutable feather impressions in the holotype.

facts.statement: Xu et al. 1999 first assigned Beipiaosaurus to the Therizinosauroidea in a very primitive position.
facts.quote: Beipiaosaurus was first assigned to the Therizinosauroidea, in a very primitive position by Xu et al. 1999.

facts.statement: According to Paul Sereno's definition of the group, Beipiaosaurus is the basal-most member of Therizinosauroidea.
facts.quote: According to the definition by Paul Sereno of this group, Beipiaosaurus is even by definition the basal most member.

facts.statement: Cau (2024) suggested that Jianchangosaurus is a junior synonym of Beipiaosaurus because the distinguishing diagnosis was based on ontogenetically variable characters.
facts.quote: Cau (2024) suggested that the contemporary Jianchangosaurus represents a junior synonym of Beipiaosaurus, since the diagnosis distinguishing the taxa was based on ontogenetically variable characters.

facts.statement: In 2018, McNamara and colleagues discovered fossilized skin flakes from Beipiaosaurus using a scanning electron microscope.
facts.quote: In 2018, McNamara and colleagues discovered the fossilised remains of skin flakes from numerous feathered dinosaurs from the Jehol Biota and some bird species using scanning electron microscope on the preserved feather impressions.

facts.statement: Corneocyte structures indicate that non-avian dinosaurs like Beipiaosaurus shed their skin as dandruff, similar to extant birds and mammals.
facts.quote: In addition, the identified corneocytes structures seem to indicate that non-avian dinosaurs had a similar way of shedding skin to extant birds and mammals.

facts.statement: The flora of the Yixian Formation was dominated by conifers, ferns, cycads, and horsetails.
facts.quote: The flora was dominated by conifers related to modern species that are found mainly in subtropical and temperate upland forests, with the presence of ferns, cycads, and horsetails.

facts.statement: Beipiaosaurus was approximately 2.2 meters long and 0.9 meters tall, making it the second largest known feathered dinosaur.
facts.quote: Beipiaosaurus medía alrededor de 2,2 metros de largo y 0,9 de altura, por lo que se trata del segundo dinosaurio con plumas más grande conocido.

facts.statement: The estimated weight of Beipiaosaurus is approximately 85 kilograms.
facts.quote: Su peso ha sido estimado en unos 85 kg.

facts.statement: Beipiaosaurus possessed a toothless beak with teeth located in the cheek area.
facts.quote: Beipiaosaurus tenía un pico desdentado con dientes en la mejilla.

facts.statement: Beipiaosaurus had a large head relative to other tericynosaurs and shared some features with related oviraptorosaurs.
facts.quote: La cabeza era grande comparada a la de otros tericinosaurianos, y tenía algunas características similares a los relacionados oviraptorosaurianos.

facts.statement: Skin impressions show Beipiaosaurus was covered in soft feather-like fibers similar to Sinosauropteryx but longer and oriented perpendicular to the arm.
facts.quote: Las impresiones de la piel indican que su cuerpo fue cubierto por las fibras similares plumas suaves, que son parecidas a las de Sinosauropteryx, pero más largas, y orientadas perpendicularmente al brazo.

facts.statement: Beipiaosaurus uniquely possessed a secondary layer of much longer and simpler feathers emerging from the inner feather layer among known theropods.
facts.quote: Único entre los terópodos conocidos, el Beipiaosaurus también poseía una capa secundaria de plumas mucho más largas y más simples que surgían de la capa interna.

facts.statement: Xu et al. first described these unique feathers in 2009 based on a sample consisting of the torso, head, and neck.
facts.quote: Estas plumas únicas fueron descritas por primera vez por Xu et al. En 2009, a partir de una muestra constituida por el torso, la cabeza y el cuello.

facts.statement: The widest feathers in Sinosauropteryx are only 0.2 mm wide, whereas those in Beipiaosaurus are significantly wider.
facts.quote: Las plumas más amplias de Sinosauropteryx son solo de 0,2 mm de ancho y solo ligeramente más ancho en formas más grandes como Dilong.

facts.statement: None of the feathers are preserved curved beyond a wide arc, indicating they were quite rigid.
facts.quote: Ninguna se conserva curvadas o dobladas más allá de un arco ancho, indicando que eran bastante rígidas.

facts.statement: Beipiaosaurus was the largest known dinosaur with feather evidence until the discovery of Yutyrannus.
facts.quote: Beipiaosaurus fue el dinosaurio con evidencia de plumas más grande conocido hasta el descubrimiento de Yutyrannus.

facts.statement: In 1996, farmer Li Yinxian discovered a theropod dinosaur skeleton near the village of Sihetun.
facts.quote: En 1996, el campesino Li Yinxian descubrió un esqueleto de un dinosaurio terópodo cerca de la aldea de Sihetun.

facts.statement: On May 27, 1999, Nature announced the discovery, and the type species was named and described by Xu Xing, Tang Zhilu, and Wang Xiaolin as Beipiaosaurus inexpectus.
facts.quote: El 27 de mayo de 1999 la revista Nature, anunció el descubrimiento la especie tipo fue nombrada y descrita por Xu Xing, Tang Zhilu y Wang Xiaolin como Beipiaosaurus inexpectus.

facts.statement: Beipiaosaurus lived at the beginning of the Cretaceous period, approximately 130 to 125 million years ago between the Barremian and Aptian stages, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a principio del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 130 a 125 millones de años entre el Barremiense y el Aptiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Xu et al. suggest that Beipiaosaurus feathers represent an intermediate stage between Sinosauropteryx and more advanced birds (Avialae).
facts.quote: Xu et al. sugieren que las plumas de Beipiaosaurus representen una etapa intermedia entre Sinosauropteryx y pájaros más avanzados (Avialae).

facts.statement: In a 2009 interview, Xu stated that neither type of feather was definitely for flight and researchers were unsure if they were for display or other functions.
facts.quote: En una entrevista de 2009, Xu declaró: "Ambos tipos de plumas definitivamente no son para el vuelo, inferir la función de algunas estructuras de los animales extintos sería muy difícil, y en este caso, no estamos muy seguros de si estas plumas son para la exhibición O algunas otras funciones."

facts.statement: It is speculated that the finer feathers served as insulation and the larger feathers were ornamental, perhaps for social interactions like mating or communication.
facts.quote: Se especula que las plumas más finas servían como capa aislante y que las plumas más grandes eran ornamentales, tal vez para interacciones sociales como el apareamiento o la comunicación.

facts.statement: The specimen was collected from sediments deposited during the Aptian stage of the Cretaceous, approximately 125 to 124 million years ago.
facts.quote: El espécimen fue recolectado en sedimentos depositados durante la etapa aptiana del Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 125 a 124 millones de años atrás.

facts.statement: The type specimen is housed in the collection of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing, China.
facts.quote: Este espécimen se encuentra en la colección del Instituto de Paleontología Vertebrada y Paleoantropología, en Beijing, China.

facts.statement: The type specimen consists of a partial, sub-adult skeleton that is widely disarticulated.
facts.quote: Se compone de un esqueleto parcial, sub-adulto, que está ampliamente desarticulado.

facts.statement: A significant number of fossilized bones were recovered, including cranial fragments.
facts.quote: Se recuperó un número significativo de huesos fosilizados, incluyendo, fragmentos craneales.

facts.statement: A second partial skeleton, STM 31-1, was described by Xu et al. in 2009 and preserved a significant coverage of unique, elongated feathers.
facts.quote: Un segundo espécimen, STM 31-1, un esqueleto parcial, fue descrito por Xu et al. En 2009, que preservó una cobertura significativa de plumas únicas y alargadas.

facts.statement: The back of the skull in the second specimen was damaged.
facts.quote: La parte posterior del cráneo de este espécimen fue maltratada.

facts.statement: Beipiaosaurus was originally assigned to Therizinosauroidea in a basal position by Xu et al. in 1999.
facts.quote: Beipiaosaurus fue asignado desde el principio a Therizinosauroidea, en una posición basal, por Xu et al. en 1999.

facts.statement: All subsequent phylogenetic analyses have confirmed this assignment.
facts.quote: Todos los análisis filogenéticos posteriores han confirmado esta asignación.

facts.statement: According to Paul Sereno's definition of the group, Beipiaosaurus is by definition the most basal member.
facts.quote: Según la definición de Paul Sereno de este grupo, Beipiaosaurus es incluso por definición, el basal más miembro.

facts.statement: In 2010, Zanno noted that Beipiaosaurus shares a sister-taxon relationship with a clade including all more derived therizinosauroids.
facts.quote: Zanno en 2010 señaló que Beipiaosaurus comparte una relación taxón hermano con un taxón que incluye todos los derivados más derivados de los terizinosáuroides.

facts.statement: Zanno also concluded that there is a genus less derived than Beipiaosaurus, the genus Falcarius, which is a basal Therizinosauria outside Therizinosauroidea.
facts.quote: Zanno también concluyó que hay un género que es menos derivado que Beipiaosaurus , el género Falcarius, que es un Therizinosauria basal por fuera de Therizinosauroidea.

facts.statement: As a primitive Therizinosauria, Beipiaosaurus has characteristics suggesting all therizinosaurs, including derived Therizinosauridae, should be included within Theropoda Coelurosauria rather than Sauropodomorpha or Ornithischian relatives as once postulated.
facts.quote: Beipiaosaurus, siendo considerado para ser un Therizinosauria primitivo, tiene características que sugieran que todos los tericinosáuridos, incluyendo los derivado Therizinosauridae, deben incluirse dentro de los Theropoda Coelurosauria y no Sauropodomorpha o parientes de Ornithischia según lo postulado alguna vez.

facts.statement: The time range for Beipiaosaurus is from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group for Beipiaosaurus is Therizinosauroidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Therizinosauroidea

facts.statement: Beipiaosaurus is classified in the class Reptilia.

facts.statement: There are two recorded fossil occurrences of Beipiaosaurus.

facts.quote: Los estudios sugieren que el paleoambiente de la Formación Yixian tenía fluctuaciones estacionales del clima, y era cálido y húmedo, con estaciones secas, en las que el ambiente se volvía más árido.

facts.statement: The mean annual temperature during the time of Beipiaosaurus was 10 degrees Celsius, with relatively cold winters for the generally warm Mesozoic era.
facts.quote: La temperatura media anual durante el tiempo de Beipiaosaurus fue de 10 grados centígrados, con inviernos relativamente fríos para la época generalmente mesozoica caliente.

facts.statement: A 2013 study by Wu et al. concluded that orbital forcing, the effect on climate caused by changes in Earth's axial tilt and orbit shape, contributed to the climate fluctuations of this formation.
facts.quote: Un estudio de Wu et al. de 2013 concluyó que el forzamiento orbital, que es el efecto sobre el clima causado por cambios en la inclinación del eje de la Tierra y por la forma de la órbita de la Tierra, contribuyó a las fluctuaciones climáticas de esta formación.

facts.statement: The flora was dominated by conifers related to modern species found mainly in subtropical and temperate highland forests, with the presence of ferns, cycads, and horsetails.
facts.quote: La flora estaba dominada por coníferas relacionadas con especies modernas que se encuentran principalmente en los bosques de tierras altas subtropicales y templados , con la presencia de helechos, cicas y colas de caballo.
